litres.label: measured

To cut fuel at the arable sites, you can implement several changes based on published research, such as shifting up and throttling back, reducing tillage, or correcting tyre pressures. Because these ideas overlap, their savings should not be added together.

Here are the top four opportunities:

*   **Shift up and throttle back**: Backed by strong evidence from *Shift Up and Throttle Back to Save Tractor Fuel (PM 2089)*, *Analysis of Nebraska tractor test data (MicroCAD 2025)*, and *Reduction Rates of Fuel Consumption by Gear Up and Throttle Down on an Agricultural Tractor*. This is estimated to save 352 to 1,645 litres of fuel (estimated), avoiding 1.2 to 5.6 tonnes of CO2e (estimated) and saving £253 to £1,935 in fuel costs (estimated) per year.
*   **Reduced or conservation tillage**: Backed by strong evidence from *Košutić et al. 2007 — conservation tillage (type II) winter wheat*, *Conservation tillage vs plough (flow-meter measurement)*, and *Reduced tillage vs deep ploughing maize. Energy 69 (2014) 227-235*. This is estimated to save 338 to 1,673 litres of fuel (estimated), avoiding 1.1 to 5.7 tonnes of CO2e (estimated) and saving £243 to £1,967 in fuel costs (estimated) per year.
*   **No-till**: Backed by moderate evidence from *Košutić et al. 2007 — no-till winter wheat* and *The Economic Advantages of No-Till: Diesel Fuel (citing Hanna et al. 2001)*. This is estimated to save 2,428 to 3,156 litres of fuel (estimated), avoiding 8.2 to 10.7 tonnes of CO2e (estimated) and saving £1,743 to £3,711 in fuel costs (estimated) per year.
*   **Correct tyre pressure**: Backed by moderate evidence from *Tyre pressure and ballast effects on tractor fuel use*, *Tuned front/rear tyre pressure*, and *Correct tyre pressures save fuel and time (field test 2023)*. The arable site in Bavaria should first adopt **Shift up / throttle down** or **Reduced / conservation tillage**, as both practices have the strongest evidence for saving fuel. 

*   **Shift up / throttle down** has strong evidence from *Shift Up and Throttle Back to Save Tractor Fuel (PM 2089)*, *Analysis of Nebraska tractor test data (MicroCAD 2025)*, and *Reduction Rates of Fuel Consumption by Gear Up and Throttle Down on an Agricultural Tractor*. It is estimated to save 322 to 1,505 litres of fuel (estimated), 1.1 to 5.1 tonnes of CO2e (estimated), and £231 to £1,770 (estimated) in fuel costs per year.
*   **Reduced / conservation tillage** has strong evidence from *Košutić et al. 2007 — conservation tillage (type II) winter wheat*, *Conservation tillage vs plough (flow-meter measurement)*, and *Reduced tillage vs deep ploughing maize. Energy 69 (2014) 227-235*. It is estimated to save 304 to 1,506 litres of fuel (estimated), 1.0 to 5.1 tonnes of CO2e (estimated), and £218 to £1,771 (estimated) in fuel costs per year.
*   **No-till** has moderate evidence from *Košutić et al. 2007 — no-till winter wheat* and *The Economic Advantages of No-Till: Diesel Fuel (citing Hanna et al. 2001)*. It offers even larger estimated savings of 2,240 to 2,912 litres of fuel (estimated), 7.6 to 9.8 tonnes of CO2e (estimated), and £1,609 to £3,425 (estimated) in fuel costs per year.
*   For the tillage site in Konya, **Shift up / throttle down** is estimated to save 30 to 140 litres of fuel (estimated) and £22 to £165 (estimated) per year, while **Reduced / conservation tillage** is estimated to save 34 to 167 litres of fuel (estimated) and £24 to £196 (estimated) per year.

Please note that these savings are estimates, never guarantees. Any differences in fuel use are things to investigate, not proof of a fault, waste, or loss.

**Next step:** Review tractor driving techniques with your team to encourage shifting up and throttling back during lighter operations.
